★ Tourist FAQ ★
Am I really eligible? I'm just here on holiday.

Yes. The promotion is open to anyone aged 18+ residing in or visiting the Philippines at the time of ticket purchase. You must hold a valid government photo ID (your passport works) and be able to receive prize payouts in the Philippines if you win — either by visiting in person within 28 days, or via Philippine bank/GCash account for the cash alternative.

What if I win and I'm already back home?

Two options: (a) fly back within 28 days of the draw to collect the bike in person, with LTO paperwork in your legal name; or (b) elect the 75% cash alternative within the original 14-day claim window — paid to an account in your legal name, within reasonable time and subject to clearance. Most foreign winners choose the cash option.

How do I prove I bought the ticket?

You'll receive SMS and email confirmation with your unique serial ticket numbers immediately after payment clears. Keep both. If you win, you'll present the confirmation along with your passport ID matching the name you used at purchase.

Is this gambling? Will I get in trouble at home?

No. This is a permitted sales promotion under Philippine consumer law (RA 7394), regulated by the Department of Trade and Industry — not gambling under PAGCOR or PCSO sweepstakes. It's the same legal category as bank promotional raffles (BPI, BDO, etc.). Whether it complies with your home country's laws is your responsibility — but participation itself is fully legal in the Philippines.

Can I buy a ticket before I arrive in the Philippines?

No. You must be physically in the Philippines at the time of ticket purchase. Tickets bought from outside the country may be voided. The simplest route: scan the QR code when you arrive on the island, in your hotel room, at the bar, or anywhere else you see our branding.

What does my money actually fund?

Net proceeds (after prize cost, tax, and operating costs) go to the Kuya Lifesaver Foundation — a Philippine non-stock non-profit funding the "Sea Ambulance" rescue vessel and emergency response equipment across Boracay and surrounding islands. Quarterly donation reports are published on the website. The amount donated per draw is set out in the DTI permit and shown on the ticket page.

What if the draw is rigged?

Every draw is conducted live on Facebook in the presence of a DTI representative, using a certified Random Number Generator. The DTI rep signs the Minute of Drawing and the Winner. The draw is recorded and the recording stays online indefinitely. If anything looks off, you can file a complaint directly with DTI Fair Trade Enforcement Bureau (fteb@dti.gov.ph) — they investigate.
